title: Gold 30m: volume has dried up inside the triangle. Coiling for a move or just losing interest?
author: FarInspector1873
selftext:
Gold (XAU/USDT), 30m (Nov 12–14).

Price has made lower highs for about two days against a flat floor near 3,873. The falling upper line has 9 marked touches and the floor only 3. Price is now sitting right at the upper line around 3,885, so the gap between the two lines is only about 10–12 points. Volume has also faded since a spike on Nov 13.

I'm not sure how much to read into it. Descending triangles are usually described as bearish, but this one has gone a long time without resolving, and a squeeze this tight can break either way.

A few things I can't settle:

* Does the long time without a break make the triangle more reliable or less?
* Would you wait for a full 30m close beyond a line, or for a retest first?
* Does the very low volume mean a move is coming, or just a quiet weekend session?

How do you handle triangles on gold at this size?

Not a call either way, just a chart I'm watching.

comments.author: Ok_Map5721
comments.body:
on the volume question, it's mostly the weekend, and for gold that matters more than usual. XAU/USDT is a perp on a market that's closed: COMEX gold stops Friday evening and reopens Sunday \~23:00 UTC. from Friday close until then the perp is just trading against its own book with no real gold price behind it, so volume dries up and lines drawn on that stretch are mostly noise from a thin book.

what actually decides the move is usually the reopen: futures open wherever the weekend news put them, and the perp snaps to that. so I wouldn't read much into a weekend triangle breaking either way. I'd watch where gold opens Sunday night, and treat any weekend break with a lot of suspicion.

on the triangle itself: if you want to know whether descending triangles work on gold, the honest way is to define the pattern by fixed rules, find every instance in a few years of data, and compare what happens after with random times. one chart will look convincing either way.

comments.author: AoideusWasBanned
comments.body: I'd take the full 30m close over waiting for a retest. On fast breaks the clean retest often never comes and you just watch it go. But on a weekend perp I wouldn't trust any of these lines until the Sunday reopen anyway.
